title: Observability: token-level cost/latency dashboards + KV cache tracing/logging + alert tuning
author: Priya Patel
description: Context: production teams observed noisy alerts and poor visibility into token-level cost/latency breakdowns and KV cache behavior during peak traffic. This PR delivers (1) token-level cost/latency Grafana dashboards with precalculated P50/P95/P99 series and per-model breakdown, (2) KV cache tracing spans and enhanced logging to link cache hits/misses to request traces, and (3) alert tuning to reduce noise while preserving SLO protection. Motivation: reduce incident MTTR by making token-unit economics visible, and reduce alert fatigue caused by transient KV spikes. Changes: - Add token-level dashboard JSON with queries for redwood.inference.token_cost_per_request, redwood.inference.token_latency_{p50,p95,p99}, redwood.inference.tokens_per_request, and model label breakdowns. - Add KV cache dashboard panel and tracing helpers: capture redwood.kv.cache_hit_ratio, redwood.kv.kv_fetch_latency_p50/p95/p99, and annotate panels with traced request IDs. - Add Prometheus alert rule refinements: move kv_fetch_latency_p99 alert to a sustained 5m burn-rate evaluation, raise threshold for p99 from 200ms to 600ms for GPUDedicated pools, and add a new low-severity alert for sudden token-cost delta (5%+ increase sustained 10m) to detect cost regressions. - Instrumentation: telemetry/metrics: expose token_cost_per_request as histogram with exemplar linking to trace id; tracing: attach cache.hit/miss events to request spans; logging: structured K/V for cache keys and fetch latency. - Tests: add dashboard smoke test and alert rule unit tests that run against test Prometheus snapshot. Rollout: dashboards staged to grafana/dev then promoted to grafana/prod via the standard dashboard-operator. Alerts deployed to staging for 48h with SRE monitoring before prod rollout. Backout plan: revert alert rule file and rollback dashboard via operator if regressions/false negatives are observed. No breaking API changes. See linked Linear items for rollout checklist and telemetry QA tasks.

review_conversation: Alex Kim (reviewer): Nice work. A couple of asks: 1) can we include exemplar linking from the histogram so traces show in Grafana panels? 2) The kv_fetch_latency threshold seems low for Dedicated pools — can you justify or widen?

Priya (author): Added exemplar support in token_metrics.go and updated panels to use exemplars. Raised p99 threshold for Dedicated pools to 600ms and switched the alert to a 5m burn-rate policy to avoid flapping.
Jordan Lee (reviewer): Please add a test that validates the new alert logic doesn't fire on synthetic load in staging. Also confirm the dashboard performs with large label cardinality (per-model).

Priya (author): Added tests/observability/test_dashboards.py to load a Prometheus snapshot and validate rules. Dashboard uses a top-N per-model aggregation and a fallback per-tenant summary to keep panels performant.
Samir Gupta (approver): Verified alert behavior in staging for 48h, noise reduced by ~70% while still catching real regressions. Approving for merge.
